applies_why: Yes: the judge resolves the Acts 2:30 clash by treating that single verse's silence about the channel as decisive, instead of weighing the pressed chain against the link by footing.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase 'never verse by verse' — one reading allows deciding a single verse is underdetermined because it does not name the channel; the other requires judging the pressed chain's support by footing as a whole even if no verse states the point word for word.
why: The judge makes the single verse's silence about whose body is the channel decisive, which is the verse-by-verse/stating-verse approach K-C retires when the pressed witnesses are the pressing side's chain read together.
